content.value_statement: Teams often choose API styles without a clear decision process. This skill guides REST, GraphQL, tRPC, versioning, responses, auth, rate limits, and security checks.
actual_capabilities: Compares REST, GraphQL, tRPC, WebSocket, and gRPC using consumer and data needs.
Guides REST resource naming, HTTP method choice, and status code selection.
Explains response envelopes, error response fields, and pagination tradeoffs.
Summarizes authentication, versioning, rate limiting, and documentation decisions.
Lists GraphQL and tRPC fit criteria with security and integration considerations.
Includes an optional local validator for OpenAPI files and common API code issues.
limitations: It gives design guidance, not complete framework-specific implementation code.
The validator is heuristic and checks only a limited set of local API files.
Security testing guidance is for authorized systems only.
It does not replace threat modeling, penetration testing, or legal review.

use_cases.title: Choose an API Style
use_cases.description: Compare REST, GraphQL, tRPC, WebSocket, and gRPC for a new product or service boundary.

use_cases.title: Standardize API Design
use_cases.description: Create consistent endpoint naming, response formats, versioning, auth, and rate limit conventions.

use_cases.title: Review API Security Basics
use_cases.description: Check authentication, authorization, validation, GraphQL controls, and configuration before release.

prompt_templates.title: Pick an API Style
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to choose between REST, GraphQL, and tRPC for my application. Ask about consumers, data complexity, caching, and team constraints first.

prompt_templates.title: Design REST Endpoints
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design REST resources for my domain. Recommend resource names, HTTP methods, status codes, pagination, and error response rules.

prompt_templates.title: Plan API Evolution
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan versioning, authentication, rate limits, and documentation for a public API with multiple clients.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an API Proposal
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my API proposal for style fit, response consistency, authorization gaps, validation coverage, and documentation completeness.

output_examples.input: A TypeScript monorepo needs an internal admin API for a single web client.
output: Recommendation: tRPC is a strong fit because both client and server use TypeScript.
Tradeoff: avoid tRPC if non-TypeScript clients or public API consumers are expected.
Next steps: define procedures, shared types, authentication, and rate limit expectations.

output_examples.input: A public partner API needs predictable endpoints and external documentation.
output: Recommendation: REST with OpenAPI provides broad compatibility and clear documentation.
Use plural resources, standard HTTP methods, explicit status codes, and stable versioning.
Add error formats, pagination rules, authentication guidance, and rate limit headers.

output_examples.input: A team wants a pre-release API security checklist.
output: Review authentication, authorization, input validation, rate limiting, GraphQL controls, and configuration.
Check BOLA, privilege boundaries, token handling, field-level access, and error disclosure.
Run only authorized tests and document remaining risks before launch.

best_practices: Start by identifying API consumers before choosing REST, GraphQL, tRPC, or another style.
Use one response and error format across endpoints unless a documented exception exists.
Plan authentication, rate limits, versioning, and documentation before public release.
anti_patterns: Do not default to REST when client needs or team constraints point to another style.
Do not expose internal errors or sensitive implementation details in API responses.
Do not run security tests against systems without explicit authorization.

faq.question: Does this skill generate production API code?
faq.answer: No. It guides API design choices and review steps. Implementation still depends on your framework and project requirements.

faq.question: Can it help choose between REST and GraphQL?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares consumer needs, data complexity, caching, client flexibility, and team readiness.

faq.question: Does it support tRPC decisions?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains when tRPC fits TypeScript monorepos and when public or multi-language APIs need another approach.

faq.question: What does the validator script do?
faq.answer: It scans local API files for OpenAPI metadata, error handling, status codes, validation, auth, rate limits, and logging signals.

faq.question: Is the security testing content offensive?
faq.answer: It is written as defensive review guidance. Use it only on systems you own or are authorized to test.
